_doc: STROKEWIDTH: the FIELD-SCOPED Stroke-panel apply law, pinned across the
three LIVE implementations (the workspace_interpreter reference, Rust
jas_dioxus, Swift JasSwift). See transcripts/STROKE.md
'Panel-to-selection wiring'.
THE LAW. A Stroke-panel edit names the field the user just committed.
Only the attribute GROUP that field owns is taken from panel state; every
other stroke attribute is preserved from the element being edited, per
element. The old law rebuilt the WHOLE Stroke from panel state on every
edit, so touching any control reset a selected 5pt dashed arrowheaded
line to the panel's 1pt defaults (JYH, 2026-07-24). Vector
'arrowhead_edit_preserves_rich_width' is that exact repro and FAILS under
the old law (it yields width 1.0, not 5.0).
THE GROUPS. weight->width; cap->linecap; join->linejoin;
miter_limit->miter_limit; align_stroke->align; the dashed toggle and all
six dash/gap inputs and dash_align_anchors->the whole dash pattern (they
are one pattern and cannot be written apart); start_arrowhead->start_arrow;
end_arrowhead->end_arrow; start_arrowhead_scale->start_arrow_scale ONLY and
end_arrowhead_scale->end_arrow_scale ONLY (each scale is its own group so an
UNLINKED scale edit cannot stamp the panel's sibling scale onto the element;
the link-scales chain mirrors by COMMITTING the sibling field, which applies
through that field's own group); arrow_align->arrow_align; profile and
profile_flipped->the element's width points ONLY, leaving the Stroke
untouched. Every other panel field owns no element attribute and writes
NOTHING (link_arrowhead_scale is a UI-only flag: toggling the chain must not
push an undo step that changes nothing).
SHAPE. Each vector is language-neutral. 'op' is 'panel_edit' (the group
law) or 'color_pick' (the colour route: a colour pick changes the colour
and nothing else). 'edited' is the committed panel field key; the flat
GLOBAL form ('stroke_cap' — what a YAML `set:` effect writes) must
normalize to the same group, pinned by the *_global_key vectors.
'base' is the element's existing stroke as a flat attribute map, or the
string 'rich_stroke' naming the shared map below, or null for an element
with no stroke (which takes the vector's 'fallback' stroke instead).
'panel' is a DELTA over 'panel_defaults' below — only the fields the
vector cares about. 'expected' is likewise a DELTA merged over the
effective base (or over 'fallback' when base is null): the keys it names
are what the edit CHANGED, and every key it omits must come back
unchanged. That is the whole point of the law, so the delta form states
it directly. An 'expected' of null means NO WRITE REACHES THE DOCUMENT
(no undo step, element untouched). 'committed_width' is the
weight input's committed value and is read only by the width group.
Colours are hex; arrowhead / cap / join / align / arrow_align ids are the
snake_case workspace ids. 'dash' is the active dash array (empty = not
dashed); the ports' fixed-array + dash_len representation must present the
same active slice.

panel_defaults._comment: The Stroke panel sitting at its 1pt defaults — the state that used to be stamped over the whole selection on every edit.

rich_stroke._comment: JYH's repro element: a deliberately rich 5pt stroke where EVERY attribute differs from the panel defaults, so any whole-rebuild shows up as a diff.

vectors.name: arrowhead_edit_preserves_rich_width
vectors._comment: JYH's EXACT repro. Rich 5pt stroke selected, panel at its 1pt defaults, user picks a closed_arrow end head. Only end_arrow changes; width STAYS 5.0. Under the old whole-rebuild law width came back 1.0 (plus butt/miter/no-dash/no-start-arrow/center/10/tip_at_end/opacity 1.0) — this vector is the RED one.

vectors.name: arrowhead_edit_preserves_rich_width_global_key
vectors._comment: Same edit arriving as the flat GLOBAL key a YAML `set:` effect writes. Must normalize to the same group.

vectors.name: weight_edit_writes_only_width
vectors._comment: The weight input is the ONE field that reads committed_width. Everything else on the rich stroke survives.

vectors.name: weight_edit_from_global_key
vectors._comment: The weight global is `stroke_width`, not `stroke_weight` — it must still reach the width group.

vectors.name: align_edit_from_global_key
vectors._comment: The align global is `stroke_align` (the panel field is `align_stroke`); both forms reach the align group.

vectors.name: dash_length_edit_writes_the_whole_pattern
vectors._comment: The dash inputs are ONE group: a dash_1 edit rewrites the pattern from panel state (they cannot be written apart) and sets dash_align_anchors with it — but the width / caps / arrowheads still survive.

vectors.name: dashed_toggle_off_clears_the_pattern
vectors._comment: dashed=false empties the pattern — and nothing else. The 5pt width and both arrowheads survive.

vectors.name: start_scale_edit_writes_only_start_scale
vectors._comment: STROKEWIDTH repair 4. Each scale is its OWN group: an unlinked start-scale edit must NOT stamp the panel's end-scale (100) over the element's 75. The chain mirror does not need a wide group — it commits the sibling field, which applies through that field's own group.

vectors.name: profile_edit_leaves_the_stroke_untouched
vectors._comment: The width profile lives in the element's width points, not the Stroke, so the Stroke comes back byte-identical.

vectors.name: link_scales_toggle_writes_nothing
vectors._comment: UI-only flag: no group, so no document write at all (expected null). Toggling the chain must not push an undo step that changes nothing.

vectors.name: cap_edit_on_element_with_no_stroke_uses_the_fallback
vectors._comment: An element with no stroke takes the panel/default fallback stroke, then the edited group on top.

vectors.name: color_pick_preserves_the_rich_stroke
vectors._comment: STROKEWIDTH repair: the colour route is colour-only. Picking red on the rich stroke changes the colour and NOTHING else — the old law rebuilt a bare Stroke(color:, width:) and dropped cap/join/dash/arrowheads/align/miter/opacity.

vectors.name: color_pick_with_no_base_is_a_1pt_stroke
vectors._comment: Nothing to recolour: a plain 1pt stroke in that colour.
